segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With a muffled grunt and a flurry of powdery snow, the figure yanks its head out of the drift.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It’s a fox. A real, living, three-foot-tall fox standing on two hind paws.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He wears a heavy green detective's coat that is clearly three sizes too big for him, with brass buttons the size of saucers. A long, hand-knitted red wool scarf is wrapped around his neck so many times his snout barely pokes over the top, and a crooked tweed detective hat rests lopsidedly between two pointed, velvet-brown ears.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox shakes the snow off his whiskers, vigorously brushes white powder off his coat lapels, and clears his throat with great theatrical flair.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he speaks, his voice is surprisingly deep, carrying a ridiculously posh, exaggerated British accent:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem! Splendid! An absolutely immaculate piece of trans-dimensional navigation. Father Christmas, I presume, should be standing precisely—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox pauses. His yellow eyes slowly travel across the brick wall, the icy gravel, and settle directly on the rusted green dumpster three feet from his nose.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He squints at the graffiti on the dumpster lid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he murmurs, his ears drooping slightly.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: That is... mildly disappointing. The North Pole appears to have significantly deferred its exterior maintenance.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Down the alleyway, around the corner of the gym, you hear the sharp, rhythmic crunch of wooden boots on frozen snow:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Nutcracker pursuit patrol is coming.
